definition: A main clause is the primary part of a sentence that comes before and is related to a subordinate clause, such as an although-clause. In the example discussed in the source, the subordinate clause connects indirectly to the preceding main clause.

reasons: The packet does not support that a main clause is “the primary part of a sentence that comes before” a subordinate clause; it only describes the subordinate although-clause as forming an indirect relationship with the preceding main clause.

The definition’s claim that the subordinate clause “connects indirectly to the preceding main clause” is supported, but the rest of the characterization (primary part/comes before/definition of main clause) is not explicitly given in the packet.

The packet supports that an although-clause forms an indirect relationship with the preceding main clause, but it does not support the general definition of a main clause as “the primary part of a sentence.”
The definition adds a broad grammar claim about main clauses that is not established by the supplied source; the source only uses the term in a discourse example.
